subject: Comparing estimates in groups modelling: ML or Bootstrap confidence intervals?

messages.author: b16377403693fe8d
messages.subject: Comparing estimates in groups modelling: ML or Bootstrap confidence intervals?
parts:
Hello,

I have fitted a path model with lavaan with 3 groups, and I want to compare the estimates of the same path between groups (i.e. estimate for  a~b in group 1 with estimate for  a~b in group 2 and so on...).


As I see it, the best way is to compare estimates (i have fit the models with standardized variables) with confidence intervals. There are some packages (plspm) which do this comparison with bootstrap or permutation confidence intervals.


Mi question is:

Can I do this comparison just with the ML confidence intervals?


Best regards,

Antonio

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Comparing estimates in groups modelling: ML or Bootstrap confidence intervals?
parts:
for this to be comparable the variables that to be in the same metric for every group, if you do the stndarization for all the sample simultanously, this may not be the case, there could still be different SD at each group

Its safer if you create phantom latent variables, like this

a_ph =~ c(sd1,sd2,sd3)*a
a ~~ c(0,0,0)*a

and use std.lv=T in the cfa/sem functions. This way a_ph will be a standardize variable of a, and the differences will be represented by the factor loading which will the standard deviation for each group

Later you can label the regressions

a_ph ~ c(r1,r2,r3)*b_ph

And define differences between these regressions
dif_r12 := r1-r2
dif_r13 := r1-r3
dif_r23 := r2-r3

The p-value in the output would be the wlad test for the difference in regressions between groups

Alternatively you could fix the regression labels to be equal (a_ph ~ c(r1,r1,r3)*b_ph), and do nested model comparisons with the anova function, and test the equality of regressions with the Likelihood ratio tests
